w10_P4_002413: A test engineer at a robotics bench must report, in kN, the combined push delivered by three identical actuator frames. Every actuator on a frame drives a sled of mass 150 kg. To set the drive level, the bench software traces the curve y = 1x^2 + 2x from x = 1 to x = 3 and takes the exact area beneath that trace. It then adds 3 to that area, and the number obtained is the acceleration, in metres per second squared, given to the sled. The load cell on one actuator reads the force needed to give that 150 kg sled that acceleration. A frame carries 4 actuators, so the frame total is 4 times one actuator reading, and the 3 frames together give 3 times the frame total. A 12 L coolant tank stands beside the bench and takes no part in the calculation. What is the combined push, in kN?
w10_P4_002415: A conveyor drum at a packing plant carries a roller whose mass plate is stamped 136000 g. The plant controller traces the curve y = 4x^2 + 0x from x = 0 to x = 3 and uses the exact area under it as the acceleration, in metres per second squared, at which the roller is spun up. The drive shaft must supply the force that gives that roller that acceleration. Six identical drums run on the line, so the line force is 6 times one drum figure, and 9 N of that total is absorbed by the belt tensioner and subtracted. The maintenance log then writes what remains in kilonewtons and subtracts a further 5 in those same kilonewton units as the calibration offset. A 45 L glue reservoir feeds the line but is irrelevant here. What value, in kN, does the log record?
w10_P4_002416: On a vehicle dynamometer, a cart with a mass plate reading 36000 g is accelerated according to a stored profile. The control curve is y = 4x^3 - 5x^2, and the acceleration applied to the cart, in metres per second squared, is the slope of that curve at x = 1. The dynamometer measures the force needed to give the cart that acceleration. Nine carts are tested at once on the same rail, so the rig force is 9 times one cart figure, and the report writes that rig force in kilonewtons. Because the rail is mounted in triple, the site figure is 3 times the reported rig value, and 30 is then subtracted from it as the standing tare in those same kilonewton units. What is the site figure, in kN?
w10_P4_002418: A quality rig at an elevator works has to be characterised before sign-off. A technician solves x^2 - 8x + 12 = 0 and takes the smaller of its two roots as the base setting. Multiplying that setting by 9 gives the acceleration, in metres per second squared, to which the test car is subjected, and the car has a mass of 151 kg. The hoist cable must exert the force that gives that car that acceleration. The instrument then adds 10 N of cable preload to that force and subtracts 27 N of measured guide friction. The shaft itself is 18 m deep, a figure that does not enter this calculation. What force, in N, does the instrument finally report?
w10_P4_002421: In a bicycle-frame test cell, a sled whose mass plate reads 47000 g is driven along a rail. The controller solves x^2 - 8x + 12 = 0, takes the smaller root, and adds 4 to it; the result is the acceleration, in metres per second squared, applied to the sled. The rail actuator must provide the force that gives that sled that acceleration. From that force the software subtracts 5 N for bearing drag and then adds 15 N for the spring return. The cell finally reports the demand of all its rails together, which is 5 times that corrected per-rail figure. What is the total, in N?
w10_P4_002422: A cycling laboratory needs the total energy of motion stored in a full rack of flywheels, expressed in kJ. Each flywheel has a mass plate marked 7000 g. Each one turns at a rim speed, in metres per second, equal to the smaller root of x^2 - 6x + 8 = 0. The energy a single flywheel carries by virtue of that motion is the starting figure. There are 12 flywheels on one rack, so a rack holds 12 times the single-flywheel energy, and the laboratory runs 3 identical racks. What is the total, in kJ?
w10_P4_002426: A workshop cuts steel strip from two coils measuring 88 cm and 164 cm, using the longest whole-centimetre piece length that divides both coils exactly. A trolley of mass 56 kg is then rolled at a speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to that piece length in centimetres. The safety sheet records the energy the moving trolley carries, expressed in kilojoules. To that recorded figure the assessor adds 23 as a fixed allowance in the same kilojoule units. That result is multiplied by 8 for the 8 trolleys in a bay, and then by 6 for the 6 bays in the plant. A 250 L water tank stands in the bay and forms no part of the assessment. What is the plant total, in kJ?
w10_P4_002430: A crane depot needs the single figure, in kN, that goes on its annual load certificate. Each hoist carries a block whose mass plate reads 89000 g. The acceleration applied to the block, in metres per second squared, is worked out as 8 multiplied by the sum of 2 and 4. The hoist motor must supply the force that gives that block that acceleration. The depot has 11 hoists, so the depot force is 11 times one hoist figure, from which 29 N of standing slack is subtracted. The certificate covers 6 identical depots, so the fleet force is 6 times the depot figure. What number, in kN, goes on the certificate?
w10_P4_002432: A hangar inspection sheet ends with a single number in kilonewtons, and the inspector works towards it step by step. A trolley of mass 10 kg is accelerated at a rate, in metres per second squared, equal to the larger root of x^2 - 11x + 24 = 0. The tow bar must supply the force that gives that trolley that acceleration, and the sheet records that force in kilonewtons. The inspector then subtracts 30 from the recorded value as the standing tare, in those same kilonewton units. The final entry is 5 times the result, because 5 trolleys are towed together. What is the final entry, in kN?
w10_P4_002433: An engineering audit closes with a single energy figure, in kJ, for a whole depot. Two batches of parts, one of 37 pieces and one of 281 pieces, are packed into identical full boxes using the largest box size that divides both batch counts exactly. Adding 21 to that box size gives the launch speed, in metres per second, of a test mass of 49 kg on the depot track. The energy the moving mass carries is the base figure. There are 11 tracks in a hall, so the hall energy is 11 times the base figure, and the auditor writes that in kilojoules. The depot has 8 identical halls. What is the depot figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_002437: A foundry crane lifts a mould of mass 116 kg. The programmed acceleration, in metres per second squared, is 7 multiplied by the sum of 3 and 2. The drive must produce the force that gives that mould that acceleration, and the log writes this force in kilonewtons. Three cranes work the same bay, so the bay figure is 3 times the logged value, and the supervisor then adds 15 as a fixed allowance in those same kilonewton units. The plant total is 5 times the bay figure, since 5 bays run identically. The furnace beside the bay holds 900 L of melt, which has no bearing on this. What is the plant total, in kN?
w10_P4_002440: A tile-cutting shop has two runs of edging, 376 mm and 329 mm long, and cuts both into identical whole-millimetre pieces using the longest piece length that divides both runs exactly. Subtracting 6 from that length in millimetres gives the acceleration, in metres per second squared, of the shop test carriage. The carriage has a mass of 19 kg, and the belt must supply the force that gives it that acceleration. The controller then adds 8 N of static drag to that force. Seven carriages run side by side, so the line demand is 7 times the corrected single-carriage force. What is the line demand, in N?
w10_P4_002444: A skate-park engineer tests a dummy sled of mass 36 kg. Its release speed, in metres per second, is the smaller root of x^2 - 10x + 24 = 0. The energy the sled carries while moving at that speed is the raw reading. The rig subtracts 19 J for the losses in the release catch, and the display converts what remains to kilojoules. The engineer adds 2 in those same kilojoule units as an instrument offset. The session report covers 6 identical runs, so the session figure is 6 times the corrected value. What is the session figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_002446: A physics club report ends with one number in joules, reached as follows. A cart whose mass plate reads 29000 g is rolled at a speed, in metres per second, equal to the smaller root of x^2 - 10x + 24 = 0. The energy the moving cart carries is the starting value. From it the club subtracts 25 J lost in the launch spring. Eight carts are run in the session, so the session energy is 8 times that corrected single-cart value, and a further 3 J is then subtracted for the timing gate. What is the final number, in J?
w10_P4_002449: A drop-tower operator writes out the values of 2k - 1 for k running from 1 to 4 and adds them together. Multiplying that sum by 5 gives the impact speed, in metres per second, of the test capsule. The capsule mass plate reads 40000 g, and the energy the capsule carries at that speed is the base reading. Six capsules are dropped in a campaign, so the campaign energy is 6 times the base reading, and the summary sheet writes that in kilojoules. A standing correction of 11, in those same kilojoule units, is then subtracted. What does the summary sheet show, in kJ?
w10_P4_002450: A luge training rig launches a sled whose mass plate reads 36000 g. The launch speed, in metres per second, is the larger root of x^2 - 13x + 42 = 0. The energy the sled carries at that speed is the per-run figure. Four sleds run in each heat, so a heat energy is 4 times the per-run figure, and 9 heats make up a day, so the day energy is 9 times the heat figure. The rig meter then subtracts 2 J for the trigger circuit before showing the result in kilojoules. What does the meter show, in kJ?
w10_P4_002451: A conveyor test hall rolls trays of mass 42 kg each along its lines. The tray speed, in metres per second, is the smaller root of x^2 - 10x + 16 = 0. The energy one moving tray carries at that speed is the base amount. Each conveyor carries 12 trays, so a conveyor holds 12 times the base amount. Each hall runs 8 conveyors, each site has 11 halls, and the company operates 8 identical sites. The auditor works up from a single tray to the whole company. What is the company-wide total, in J?
w10_P4_002454: A logistics audit finishes with one number in kilojoules. Two pallets hold 178 and 369 identical cartons, and the packer bundles both using the largest bundle size that divides each count exactly. A trolley whose mass plate reads 26000 g is then pushed at a speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to that bundle size. The energy the moving trolley carries is the base figure. With 9 trolleys in a bay, the bay energy is 9 times that base figure, and the auditor writes it in kilojoules. The site has 11 identical bays. What is the site total, in kJ?
w10_P4_002460: A materials laboratory needs one number in kilonewtons for its rig certificate. A carriage of mass 19 kg is accelerated along the rail. The programmed acceleration, in metres per second squared, is found by taking 2 multiplied by the sum of 8 and 12, then adding 4 to that product. The rail motor must produce the force that gives the carriage that acceleration, and the certificate records that force in kilonewtons. Because 8 identical rails share the frame, the certificate figure is 8 times the recorded value. The laboratory chiller holds 60 L of coolant, which is not involved. What is the certificate figure, in kN?
w10_P4_002470: A haulage firm spreadsheet ends with a single value in kilonewtons. A test block whose mass plate reads 68000 g sits on the firm sled. The block acceleration, in metres per second squared, is 7 multiplied by the sum of 3 and 5. The winch must supply the force that gives that block that acceleration, and the spreadsheet enters that force in kilonewtons. Seven sleds are pulled at once, so the column total is 7 times the entered value. The spreadsheet then subtracts 16, and then a further 23, both in those same kilonewton units, for the two standing tares. What is the final value, in kN?
w10_P4_002478: A wind-tunnel log closes with one number in kilonewtons. The model cart on the balance has a mass plate reading 55000 g. Its commanded acceleration, in metres per second squared, is 5 multiplied by the sum of 6 and 5. The traverse motor must supply the force that gives the cart that acceleration, and the log writes that force in kilonewtons. With 7 carts on the traverse, the log multiplies that entry by 7, then subtracts 9 in the same kilonewton units for the balance tare. What is the closing number, in kN?
w10_P4_002485: A press shop ram is driven by a stored profile. The controller takes the exact area under the curve y = 2x^2 + 6x between x = 1 and x = 3, and that area is the acceleration, in metres per second squared, given to the ram. The ram mass plate reads 198000 g, and the hydraulics must supply the force that produces that acceleration. Four standing losses are then removed from that force in turn. They are 5 N at the guide, 26 N at the seal, 6 N at the gland, and 23 N at the return spring. What net force, in N, reaches the workpiece?
w10_P4_002486: A test-bench certificate carries one number in kilonewtons at the bottom. Two stock lots contain 115 and 279 identical bolts, and the storeman packs both into trays of the largest size that divides each lot exactly. A carriage of mass 32 kg is then accelerated at a rate, in metres per second squared, numerically equal to that tray size. The rig must apply the force that gives the carriage that acceleration, and the certificate records that force in kilonewtons. The inspector adds 11, then subtracts 30, both in those same kilonewton units, for the two calibration corrections. The bench oil sump holds 18 L and is not used here. What number stands at the bottom of the certificate, in kN?
w10_P4_002487: A factory summary sheet reports a single figure in kilonewtons. A shuttle carrying a load whose plate reads 194000 g runs along a rail. Its acceleration, in metres per second squared, is set to the number of different pairs that can be chosen from 6 available sensors, taken 2 at a time. The rail drive must supply the force that gives that load that acceleration, and the sheet enters that force in kilonewtons. A fixed 30, in the same kilonewton units, is added to the entry; the result is multiplied by 3 for the 3 shuttles per line and then by 8 for the 8 lines. The rail lubricant tank holds 15 L, which is not involved. What figure does the summary sheet report, in kN?
w10_P4_002491: A laboratory report ends with one number in kilojoules. A trolley of mass 39 kg moves along a bench at a speed, in metres per second, equal to the exact area under the curve y = 1x^2 + 3x between x = 0 and x = 1. The energy the trolley carries because of that motion is the starting quantity. The technician adds 29 J to it for the energy already stored in the launch spring. That sum is then multiplied by 12, because 12 identical trolleys sit on the bench. The final line converts the result to kilojoules. A 7 L bottle of solvent stands on the same bench and plays no part. What is the number at the end of the report, in kJ?
